title: Cap. 5 Mem. 2 Scripture elect Resp: Election wills justification in time, not coeternal with election
pass_a_gloss: Response. It is one thing to elect someone to life before the foundation of the world, another to actually justify and reconcile the same person to himself before the foundation of the world. Election names in God an eternal will of justifying, reconciling, and saving the elect person, but of justifying, reconciling, and saving him in his own time through faith. Therefore the actual justification, reconciliation, and sanctification of the elect human flows from eternal election, but is not coeternal with it. It is easy to gather this from the whole Pauline discourse in that first chapter to the Ephesians. He affirms us elect before the foundations of the world were laid (Ephesians 1:4), but he does not say that we were therefore sanctified before the foundations of the world were laid, but elect that we might be holy and blameless before him in love. Nor by virtue of eternal election does he teach that we were from eternity justified or reconciled, but in the dispensation of the fullness of time, after we applied faith to the Gospel made open, verses 9, 10, and following.
pass_b_english: Response. Electing someone to life before the world’s foundation is one thing; actually justifying and reconciling that same person to himself before the world’s foundation is another. Election names in God an eternal will to justify, reconcile, and save the elect person—but to justify, reconcile, and save him in his own time through faith. So the elect person’s actual justification, reconciliation, and sanctification flow from eternal election; they are not coeternal with it. That is easy to gather from Paul’s whole argument in Ephesians 1. He affirms that we were elect before the world’s foundations were laid (Ephesians 1:4), yet he does not say we were therefore sanctified before those foundations were laid. He says we were elect so that we might be holy and blameless before him in love. Nor does he teach, by the power of eternal election, that we were justified or reconciled from eternity. He teaches that this happened in the dispensation of the fullness of time, after we applied faith to the gospel that had been opened (Ephesians 1:9–10 and following).
source_text: Resp. Aliud est eligere aliquem ad vitam ante constitutionem mundi, aliud actu justificare & reconciliare eundem sibi ante constitutionem mundi. Electio dicit in Deo aeternam voluntatem justificandi, reconciliandi & salvandi personam electam, sed justificandi, reconciliandi & salvandi suo tempore per fidem. Ipsa igitur actualis justificatio, reconciliatio, sanctificatio hominis electi fluit ab aeterna electione, sed non est eidem coaeterna. Facile est hoc colligere ex toto discursu Paulino in illo primo capite ad Ephesios. Affirmat nos electos ante jacta mundi fundamenta, vers. 4. sed non dicit proinde nos sanctificatos ante jacta mundi fundamenta, sed electos ut essemus sancti & inculpati coram eo per charitatem. Neque virtute aeternae electionis docet nos ab aeterno fuisse justificatos aut reconciliatos, sed in pleni temporis dispensatione, postquam patefacto Evangelio fidem adhibuimus, vers. 9, 10, &c.
